title: Trace Anchors and Kernel Atlas for Prefill/Decode Scheduling
creator: Mei Chen
description: Goal: produce a low-noise, high-fidelity telemetry surface that connects high-level scheduling decisions (prefill vs decode), attention pathway variants, and the concrete kernel invocations on the GPU. We will introduce the concept of Trace Anchors (lightweight span markers that denote scheduling boundaries and heuristic choices) and a Kernel Atlas (canonical naming + attributes for every kernel variant we might select). The outcome should make it straightforward to attribute latency and token-cost regressions to either scheduler heuristics, attention optimizations, or specific kernel variants. This ticket covers the design, minimal runtime changes, and dashboarding/alerting for the first rollout across a subset of models (gpt-like 16k and 32k families).
acceptance_criteria: New NVTX span conventions and JSON span tags documented and verified in a local end-to-end run
Runtime emits Trace Anchor spans at: request-start, scheduling-decision, prefill-start, prefill-end, decode-start, decode-end
Each kernel invocation includes a Kernel Atlas tag with canonical kernel_id, kernel_variant, selector_reason, exec_id, and token_range
Per-request trace can be stitched to per-GPU kernel metrics (duration, memory, occupancy) in the APM by joining exec_id
Dashboards: per-model breakdown showing median p50/p95 latency by scheduler decision and top-3 kernel variants contributing to tail latency
Canary rollout (5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%) completes without incidents and with no >5% SLO regression for latency-sensitive tiers
notes: 2026-03-05 Mei Chen: Initial sketch and problem statement. Prefill/Decode transitions are currently opaque in traces; operators must correlate GPU kernel records manually.

2026-03-07 Carlos Rivera: Proposed lightweight exec_id (uuid per logical kernel run) to avoid overloading spans with large JSON payloads. Exec_id will be recorded both on trace and emitted to per-kernel metrics sink.
2026-03-09 Performance trade-off: adding NVTX push/pop with small tags has ~0.6% overhead in microbenchmarks; acceptable for P1 rollout but we must gate by sampling rate for lower tiers.
2026-03-11 Design decision: Use a canonical kernel_id scheme: <arch>-<op>-<precision>-<tile>-<variant>. This balances readability and cardinality. Example: amx-attn-fp16-128x64-v3
2026-03-12 Instrumentation plan: Emit Trace Anchor spans at scheduler decision points; attach lightweight attributes: exec_id, phase, scheduler_hint, intended_batch_size, kv_cache_hit_rate_estimate.
2026-03-13 Dashboard plan: New panels in Console -> Runtime -> Kernel Atlas showing top kernel variants by cost per token and by tail latency.
2026-03-14 Carlos Rivera: Implemented runtime stub; local traces show anchors and kernel_id mapping. Next: add exporter mapping to observability collector and create dashboard queries.
kernel_naming_convention: Selector_reason values: heuristic_batching | kv_cached | attention_fused | fallback_emulation | quantized_path
Keep kernel_id cardinality bounded by limiting opt_flags to known set and using variant numbers for small tweaks
nvtx_span_map: - anchor.request_start: marks request ingress, tags: {exec_id, request_id, model, deployment, intent}
- anchor.scheduling_decision: tags: {exec_id, scheduler_policy, reason, selected_kernel_hint, batch_size, priority_tier}
- kernel.exec: NVTX range named using canonical kernel_id; tags: {exec_id, kernel_id, kernel_variant, stream_id, gpu_device, memory_mb, duration_ns}
Span sampling: sample 100% for errors and 10% for success paths by default; can increase to 50% for chosen canary models
telemetry_schema_snippets: Per-kernel metric labels: kernel_id, kernel_variant, exec_id, model, deployment, phase(prefill|decode), attention_path(fused|split)
Per-kernel metrics emitted: kernel_duration_ns (histogram), memory_alloc_mb (gauge), tokens_processed (counter), calls_total (counter), kernel_queue_wait_ns (histogram)
Trace tagging: exec_id as the join key between traces and metrics; use 128-bit short UUID encoded as hex for compactness
dashboard_queries: Example: Find top kernel_id by p95 duration in last 1h: SELECT kernel_id, quantile(0.95)(kernel_duration_ns) FROM kernel_metrics WHERE deployment='canary' AND model='gpt-16k' GROUP BY kernel_id ORDER BY p95 DESC LIMIT 10

Example: Token cost attribution by scheduler decision: SELECT scheduler_policy, sum(tokens_processed) AS tokens, sum(kernel_duration_ns)/sum(tokens_processed) AS ns_per_token FROM kernel_metrics WHERE time > now() - 1h GROUP BY scheduler_policy
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased cardinality in metrics can overwhelm the metrics store. Mitigation: canonical kernel_id reduces noise; restrict opt_flags; add cardinality guard in exporter that drops unknown flags.
Risk: Instrumentation overhead may affect tight latency SLOs. Mitigation: default sampling, ability to disable anchors per deployment, and canary rollout with telemetry-only sampling first.
Risk: Incorrect stitch keys if exec_id not propagated. Mitigation: integrate exec_id propagation tests in e2e test harness and fail CI on missing exec_id in any kernel emit
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): 100% sampling locally and in staging. Verify end-to-end trace->metrics joins with sample traces.
Phase 1 (canary): Deploy to 5% of traffic for two small models (gpt-8k and gpt-16k) with 50% sampling. Monitor latency SLOs and metrics cardinality for 72h.
Phase 2: Expand to 25% traffic, sampling 25%. Add alert: kernel_metrics.cardinality_growth > 25% triggers rollback.
Phase 3: 100% rollout with default sampling (10%) and dashboarding enabled for operators
comments: Mei Chen 2026-03-06: Noted that attention_path tag should allow two values: fused | split. This is important for attribution of attention-optimization regressions.
